## Purpose and scope

This protocol isolates genomic DNA from the guts of honey bees (*Apis mellifera*), pooled in groups of three individuals, for analyses of the gut community (e.g. gut symbionts). It uses surface disinfection of the cuticle, aseptic dissection, enzymatic digestion, bead beating and the NZY Soil gDNA Isolation Kit, which removes PCR inhibitors.

## Principle

Bee cuticles are disinfected with dilute sodium hypochlorite to remove external DNA. Guts are dissected aseptically and digested with Proteinase K in Buffer NSL1, then disrupted by bead beating. Contaminants are precipitated (Buffer NSL3) and removed with an inhibitor-removal column; DNA is bound to a silica column, washed, dried and eluted in preheated Buffer NSE (NZYtech, NZY Soil gDNA Isolation kit).

## Reagent preparation

- **Sodium hypochlorite 0.05%:** [TO CONFIRM: dilution from the stock, preparation frequency].
- **Buffer NSE:** add the necessary amount (40 µL per sample) to a separate tube and preheat at 56 °C.

## Procedure

### Before starting

{{< include ../../includes/_contamination-control.qmd >}}
- Include an extraction blank [TO CONFIRM: number per batch].

### 1. Sample preparation

(@) Remove the bees from the −80 °C freezer and put them in groups of three individuals in 1.5 mL disposable centrifuge tubes. Keep the tubes at 0–4 °C until disinfection.
(@) Disinfect the cuticles: soak each group of three bees for 2–3 min in 0.05% aqueous sodium hypochlorite (or 1% household bleach), then rinse three to five times in distilled water. If necessary, remove excess water from the bodies.
(@) Add 180 µL of Buffer NSL1 plus 20 µL of Proteinase K to a 1.5 mL tube and mix gently.
(@) Dissect the bees with flame-sterilised tools under aseptic conditions and on ice.
(@) Remove the guts and submerge them, by group of three bees, in the Buffer NSL1 + Proteinase K mixture.
(@) Vortex for 5 s. Incubate for 2 h at 56 °C.
(@) Vortex for 5 s. Centrifuge at 3 000 × g for 20 s.
(@) Add 500 µL of Buffer NSL1 to an NZYSpin Soil Bead Tube and transfer the sample into it by pipetting.

### 2. Sample lysis

(@) Add 150 µL of NS Enhancer and close the cap.
(@) Place the bead tube in the BeadBlaster 24R and run [TO CONFIRM: BeadBlaster 24R programme — speed, time, number of cycles and pause].

### 3. Contaminant precipitation

(@) Centrifuge for 2 min at 11 000 × g to eliminate the foam.
(@) Add 150 µL of Buffer NSL3 and vortex for 5 s. Incubate for 5 min at 0–4 °C. Centrifuge for 1 min at 11 000 × g.

### 4. Lysate filtration

(@) Load up to 700 µL of supernatant onto an NZYSpin Soil Inhibitor Removal Column (red ring) in a 2 mL collection tube. Centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 1 min and discard the column. If there is more than 700 µL, load the rest through the column in a new collection tube and combine the flow-throughs. If a pellet is present in the flow-through, transfer the supernatant to another collection tube.

### 5. DNA binding

(@) Add 250 µL of Buffer NSB and vortex for 5 s.
(@) Load 550 µL of sample onto an NZYSpin Soil Column (green ring) in a collection tube. Centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 1 min. Discard the flow-through. Load the remaining sample and repeat.

### 6. Washing and drying

(@) Add 500 µL of Buffer NSB, centrifuge for 50 s at 11 000 × g and discard the flow-through.
(@) Add 550 µL of Buffer NSW1, centrifuge for 30 s at 11 000 × g and discard the flow-through.
(@) Add 700 µL of Buffer NSW2, close the lid, vortex for 2 s and centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 30 s. Discard the flow-through and repeat this step once.
(@) Dry the membrane: centrifuge for a further 2 min at 11 000 × g.

### 7. Elution

(@) Place the column in a clean microcentrifuge tube and add 40 µL of Buffer NSE (preheated at 56 °C).
(@) Incubate with the lid open for 1 min at room temperature. Close the lid and centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 30 s.

## Calculations

Not applicable: volumes are per sample. For $n$ samples, prepare $V = v \times n \times 1.1$ of each buffer ($v$: volume per sample, µL; 1.1: 10% excess).

## Safety and waste

{{< include ../../includes/_safety-general.qmd >}}

- Sodium hypochlorite is corrosive; never mix it with the kit buffers or their waste.
- Take care with open flames when sterilising dissection tools.
{{< include ../../includes/_safety-guanidine.qmd >}}

**Waste**

{{< include ../../includes/_waste-streams.qmd >}}

For this protocol: bee remains go to biological solid waste (black bin) [TO CONFIRM: or red bin as anatomical material]; column flow-through to biological liquid waste (jerrican); used hypochlorite solution [TO CONFIRM: route].

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Solution |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Excess foam after bead beating | Detergent in the lysis buffer | Centrifuge for 2 min at 11 000 × g before adding Buffer NSL3. |
| Sample volume > 700 µL at filtration | Large lysate | Load the excess through the inhibitor-removal column in a new collection tube and combine the flow-throughs. |
| Pellet in the filtrate | Carry-over of debris | Transfer the supernatant to another collection tube. |

## Remarks

The source protocol is written for groups of three bees. Standard methods for research on honey bee gut symbionts are in the source folder for reference.

The source protocol used a FastPrep-24 5G (6.0 m/s, 30 s, one cycle, pause 300 s). The lab replaced that instrument with the BeadBlaster 24R; the BeadBlaster programme is set separately and is not a conversion of the FastPrep settings.
